title: How Can Noise Cancel Noise?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: How can headphones make silence by adding sound?
The electronics don't block the noise. They add more.
Sound is a wave of squeezed and stretched air.
A tiny microphone listens to the noise. The headphones play a copy, flipped upside down.
Where the noise squeezes the air, the copy stretches it. Together they add up to almost nothing.
But timing is everything. Half a cycle late, and the copy doubles the noise instead.
A low hum's cycle lasts just a few milliseconds. Higher sounds are faster, so the timing gets harder.
That's why it works best on steady, low hums, like an engine, and less on voices.
Two loud waves. One quiet ear.
